Glass Skin
GLASS SKIN
noun (Gen Alpha slang)
A translation of the Korean beauty term yuri pibu ("glass skin"), naming a face so clear, smooth, and dewy that it seems to reflect light like glass. The phrase went viral through Korean-beauty ("K-beauty") influencers around 2017–18, attached to multi-step skincare routines and later to photo filters that create the look artificially. For Gen Alpha girls, glass skin is the goal of the skincare routine and the look of the filtered face.

Definition · Webster 1828 · Scriptures · Corruption · Roots · Usage · Related

Biblical Definition

Glass skin means skin so smooth and shiny it looks like glass — the look girls see in videos and filters and try to copy with lots of skincare steps. The Christian observation: glass is a beautiful word in Scripture, and it is never about our faces. The heavenly city’s street "was pure gold, as it were transparent glass" (Rev 21:21) — the glory belongs to God’s dwelling. And the Bible’s best use of glass is as a mirror: "we all, with open face beholding as in a glass the glory of the Lord, are changed into the same image from glory to glory" (2Co 3:18). The face God is making glorious is the one turned toward Him. James warns about looking in a mirror and forgetting: a man "beholdeth himself, and goeth his way, and straightway forgetteth what manner of man he was" (Jas 1:24). The filtered face is a glass that lies. Real faces have pores, freckles, and lines — and every one of them is God’s handiwork. A father can tell a five-year-old: "Your skin is beautiful just the way God made it — freckles and all! The Bible says when we look at Jesus, He makes us shine on the inside." That is the only glass skin that lasts.

Webster 1828 Definition

Korean beauty ideal yuri pibu (viral c. 2017–18) of dewy, poreless skin, now a filter look — while Scripture keeps glass for God’s city and for the mirror in which we behold His glory and are changed.

GLASS SKIN, n. (K-beauty term, c. 2017–present; Gen Alpha usage) Extremely clear, smooth, luminous skin, as if made of glass; the goal of many skincare routines. "Her skin is literally glass skin."

From Korean yuri pibu, glass skin.

Related: dewy, skincare routine, Sephora kid, beauty filters.

Decode for parents: much of what children see is filtered; real skin is not glass.

Webster 1828, the root — GLASS, n. A hard, brittle, transparent, factitious substance, formed by fusing sand with fixed alkalies.

Webster 1828, the root — SKIN, n. The natural covering of animal bodies, consisting of the cuticle or scarf-skin, the rete mucosum, and the cutis or hide.

Key Scripture

Rev 21:21 — "And the twelve gates were twelve pearls; every several gate was of one pearl: and the street of the city was pure gold, as it were transparent glass."

2Co 3:18 — "But we all, with open face beholding as in a glass the glory of the Lord, are changed into the same image from glory to glory, even as by the Spirit of the Lord."

Jas 1:23 — "For if any be a hearer of the word, and not a doer, he is like unto a man beholding his natural face in a glass:"

Jas 1:24 — "For he beholdeth himself, and goeth his way, and straightway forgetteth what manner of man he was."

Modern Corruption

Glass skin sets a filtered, poreless ideal before girls whose real faces cannot meet it; Scripture keeps glass for God’s glory and the mirror that changes us into Christ’s image.

expand to see more

The ideal is not wicked in itself — clear skin is pleasant, and care is good. The trouble is that the standard is partly unreal, built from filters and editing, and children cannot tell the difference. Girls are taught to see normal skin as a flaw and to spend time, money, and worry chasing a surface that does not exist.

Tell your daughter the truth about filters, and tell her a better truth about glass. The glory Scripture promises is not on the skin but in the soul, as we behold the Lord and are changed. Pray with her in front of a mirror sometimes, thanking God for the face He made.
